titlePlain: Four Moving Parts, Repeated in a

steps.label: 1. Ansatz
steps.sub: A parameterized circuit, like RY(θ)|0>, whose parameters get tuned

steps.label: 2. Objective operator
steps.sub: A Hamiltonian or cost operator H whose expectation value you want to minimize

steps.label: 3. Quantum evaluation
steps.sub: Run the ansatz through an Estimator primitive to measure <H>

steps.label: 4. Classical update
steps.sub: A classical optimizer proposes new parameters based on what was measured

code:
from qiskit_algorithms import VQE
from qiskit_algorithms.optimizers import COBYLA
from qiskit.primitives import StatevectorEstimator
caption: VQE and COBYLA come from qiskit-algorithms; StatevectorEstimator is a core qiskit primitive.

steps.label: <H>(θ) = 0.5·cos(θ) + 0.3·sin(θ)
steps.sub: A clean closed form, not a real molecule's Hamiltonian — chosen to be checkable by hand

steps.label: Three sampled θ values
steps.sub: θ=0: 0.500000, θ=π/2: 0.300000, θ=π: -0.500000 — not monotonic, it rises slightly before it falls

steps.label: True minimum: -0.583095
steps.sub: At θ ≈ 3.6826 rad — -√(a²+b²) for H = a·Z + b·X — none of the sampled points come close

steps.label: No derivative required
steps.sub: Only the ability to evaluate <H> at chosen points — try one, see if it went up or down, adjust, repeat

steps.label: On hardware, a derivative isn't free
steps.sub: It would need extra, separate noisy measurements at shifted parameters
